key_insight: Morphology engineering enabled the first robust lateral electrical and magnetotransport measurements in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)2PbI4, revealing p-type in-plane conduction.
engineering_relevance: Controlling thin-film grain structure is a practical lever for integrating chiral perovskites into lateral spintronic and optoelectronic device architectures.
method: Engineered thin-film morphology to reduce the in-plane resistance bottleneck.
Integrated the films into Hall-bar devices for dark Hall and magnetotransport measurements.
Compared transport paths crossing grain boundaries to assess morphology effects.
evidence_signal: Hall measurements under dark conditions showed p-type conduction with ~0.2 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 mobility and ~3×10^14 cm^-2 carrier density, plus enhanced magnetoresistance across grain boundaries.
watch_item: The reported mobility is still very low and transport appears strongly grain-boundary dependent, so device performance may remain limited unless morphology is further improved.
paper_title: Morphology control and low-temperature magnetotransport in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)$_2$PbI$_4$
